merged.title: Native port scaffolding: no emulation, OpenGOAL-style set-up, port/ with hostgen, runtime, renderer and openrac-rac1
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

This takes OpenRAC from "play through emulation" to the scaffolding of a **native PC port, built the way OpenGOAL ported Jak and Daxter, for every game version**. It has three parts:

1. **No emulation.** The emulator experiment (`runtime/`) is removed. Its studies are kept in `docs/port/`, and git history keeps the code (for example at `7954152`). The launcher no longer imports ISOs or runs anything emulated.
2. **OpenGOAL's disc set-up.** `tools/extractor.py` copies and validates the player's disc, using OpenGOAL's folder layout and error numbers. The launcher's "Set up from your disc" runs it.
3. **`port/`**, the native port's code. Every version in `port/game/` is built from its decompilation into `openrac-<id>`:
   - **Ratchet & Clank (PAL)** goes furthest. `openrac-rac1-pal` loads the data from the player's executable, runs the game's own translated `main()`, and stops at the first function that has no C yet: with the public decompilation, the boot stage `func_001E99D

merged.author: PeterFarber
merged.untrustedBody:
The native PAL New Game path stops at missing crate, joint-matrix, particle, and hero routines. This adds retail-derived native implementations and corrects a stream request's callee binding so the local integration run advances through those calls. It also fixes Windows hostgen compatibility and stale renderer test expectations, allowing the committed Windows release build and all 42 CTest tests to pass.

- Implement crate initialization, joint-matrix selection, both particle allocation entries, hero animation advancement, model effects, and equipment creation, preserving EE pointer layouts and failure paths.
- Correct the stream candidate to call the existing `func_00217AE8` instead of the nonexistent overlay symbol.
- Normalize Windows source paths and newer Clang anonymous-tag and desugared type representations in hostgen. Correct CMake's translator dependency path and add a portable synthetic regression test.

merged.title: feat(rac1/pal): recover native hero movement and respawn routines
merged.author: PeterFarber
merged.untrustedBody:
The native PAL port still has missing gameplay routines after #4. This adds retail-derived implementations for hero movement, jumping, particle updates and checkpoint restoration, plus the model, map and rendering work needed along that route. A clean build using this repository's bundled PAL sources now completes a strict Veldin fall/respawn probe and can walk, jump and land after respawning.

Changes:

- Recover hero equipment attachment, pose manipulators, leaning, gait, heading/velocity, nearby-surface lookup, jump/gravity behavior, attack object queries and checkpoint restoration.
- Recover model-bank loading, moby bounds/grid/lighting, map reveal, particle dispatch/type 53 and planar speed limiting; draw vendor effect quads through the native renderer.
- Separate level controller-update wrappers from sound wrappers so input reaches gameplay.
- Add focused fixtures, input tracing and optional movie skipping for development probes. Missing-function stops remain enabled in validatio

merged.title: Match 508 functions, add a moby struct and functional C for the native port
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
This brings the fork's last stretch of work upstream. Progress goes from 3,706 to 4,214 of 5,109 functions (61.22% to 78.50% of the code), and complete units from 131 to 143.

## Matches

Around 500 functions, most of them level functions in `src/overlays`. They come from three sources:

- Our own near misses, finished off.
- Lombyte's matched C, carried over by machine where the instructions are identical and every symbol is renamed to its PAL address.
- Lombyte's C adapted where the US and PAL builds differ. Those parts were written from the PAL assembly.

The executable gains about 60 functions in `src/game` (pause menu, loaders, sky, pad, sound, transitions). Everything taken from Lombyte is listed in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` with Lombyte's name for each function.

Every match passes the full build and the audit. Nothing edits compiler output, and flags stay per file (`config/file_cflags.txt`); `tools/check_build_fidelity.py` agrees.

## Refactors

- `include/moby.h`: one moby stru

merged.title: compiler: adopt the division delay-slot barrier and the branch-group floor
merged.author: llesieur99
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

Adopt the two measured division fixes and requalify the whole published corpus
on the resulting chain. No C body, declaration, placement or matching credit is
added or changed.

- **Compiler half.** `dbr_schedule` fills delay slots with a backward scan and no
  `may_trap_p` guard, and accepts any candidate whose `dslot` attribute is "no";
  `div.s` is one. The retail build never does that — a census of the pinned image
  finds **0 of 19 806 `div.s` occupancies in a delay slot**, while integer HI/LO
  division occupies **61** — and the SDK 3.01 assembler refuses a `div.s` in a
  slot on the emitted assembly of the affected family.
  `scripts/compiler/neutralise_div_dslot.py` adds the single-precision COP1
  division/root family to the `dslot` barrier list and leaves integer division
  eligible. `cc1` moves from `5fed4e23…` to
  `4d069ae40f7e22d19bf35ccbe0b1a52973ba7f56622ce8bf85cf6d92811a6c78`;
  `gcc/config/mips/mips.md` from `177caa69…` to `9720897d…`.
- **Assembler half.*

The reconstructed chain emitted the callee-saved blocks in an order the retail
build never used. The save-block recipe forced the FPR emission block ahead of
the GPR block on saves, and the GPR block ahead of the FPR block on restores.
The released source does the opposite: `save_restore_insns` emits the GP block
first and the FP block second, in both directions. A byte-level census of the
pinned reference agrees: of the frames that save at least one GPR **and** at
least one FPR, the first save is a GPR in 92.3 % of `0_aranos_tutorial`'s 1 102

programs.

`cc1` builds of 3 October 2026 bracket it: the 00:13 build emits the GP block
first, the 06:23 build no longer does.

merged.title: compiler: fold the return-value read of the zero store and integrate its family
merged.author: llesieur99
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

The zero-store fold refuses as soon as the materialised TImode zero is read
after the store, and one reader is a read of the constant being folded. When a
body stores a TImode zero and returns 0, reload materialises the zero once in
`$v0` and the pre-reload return `(set (reg/i:SI 2 v0) (const_int 0))`
degenerates into `(use (reg/i:SI 2 v0))`. The guard then refuses, so the chain
printed `por $v0,$zero,$zero` + `sq $v0,0($base)` where the retail prints
`sq $zero,0($base)` + `move $v0,$zero`.

`fold_zero_ti_return_value.py` keeps the rule and adds exactly one bounded case:

opened.title: compiler: fold the return-value read of the zero store and integrate its family
opened.author: llesieur99
opened.untrustedBody:
## Summary

The zero-store fold refuses as soon as the materialised TImode zero is read
after the store, and one reader is a read of the constant being folded. When a
body stores a TImode zero and returns 0, reload materialises the zero once in
`$v0` and the pre-reload return `(set (reg/i:SI 2 v0) (const_int 0))`
degenerates into `(use (reg/i:SI 2 v0))`. The guard then refuses, so the chain
printed `por $v0,$zero,$zero` + `sq $v0,0($base)` where the retail prints
`sq $zero,0($base)` + `move $v0,$zero`.

`fold_zero_ti_return_value.py` keeps the rule and adds exactly one bounded case:
an exact `(use (reg/i ...))` pattern, the same register, `REG_FUNCTION_VALUE_P`
set, no jump or call between the store and the use, and a single such use. The
store folds to architectural zero and the `use` is rewritten to a plain
`(set (reg/i:SI 2 v0) (const_int 0))`; both changes share one
`validate_change`/`apply_change_group` group, so an unrecognised pattern
abandons the whole group and nothing is fold
